#### 1. Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.480)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5617472, Reactome:R-HSA-9616222)

**Proposed mechanism:** RARA pathogenic variant —DISRUPTS→ RARA (HGNC:9752); RARA (HGNC:9752) —INCREASES→ aberrant retinoic acid signaling (REACT:R-HSA-70183); aberrant retinoic acid signaling (REACT:R-HSA-70183) —LEADS_TO→ gene transcription regulation (GO:0006351); gene transcription regulation (GO:0006351) —LEADS_TO→ intellectual disability (HP:0001249); H3-3A pathogenic variant —DISRUPTS→ H3-3A (HGNC:29904); H3-3A (HGNC:29904) —INCREASES→ histone modification (GO:0016569); histone modification (GO:0016569) —LEADS_TO→ gene transcription regulation (GO:0006351); gene transcription regulation (GO:0006351) —LEADS_TO→ developmental delay (HP:0001263). Gain-of-function mutations in RARA lead to aberrant retinoic acid signaling and dysregulated gene transcription, contributing to intellectual disability in MONDO:0012883. Similarly, gain-of-function mutations in H3-3A disrupt normal histone modifications, consequently affecting gene transcription and causing developmental delay in Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1. Both pathways converge on the central process of gene transcription regulation.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in RARA or H3-3A with a clear loss-of-function effect, or demonstration that the identified variants do not alter histone modification or transcription factor activity, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Presence of high-frequency (AF > 0.01) non-synonymous variants in RARA or H3-3A in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this mechanistic link could pave the way for targeted therapies that modulate histone modification or retinoic acid signaling to ameliorate neurodevelopmental deficits in both conditions.
